title: Model ingest pipeline: staged compaction and tokenizer adapter decoupling
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Rationalize the model ingestion pipeline to reduce tail latency and simplify tokenizer lifecycle. Deliver a staged shard compaction service, a tokenizer-adapter registry that decouples lexicon initialization from weight hydration, and migration tooling to convert legacy manifests into the canonical meta format used by the new loader.
background: Over the last 18 months we accumulated a set of loader variants to support multiple weight formats and various sharding strategies. As a result: (1) model startup latency and memory spikes are inconsistent across customers, (2) tokenizer initialization is tightly coupled into the weight activation path which prevents lightweight cold-starts for text-only endpoints, and (3) several legacy manifest formats are still supported in-line which increases code complexity and maintenance burden. Recent incidents (see incident notes) showed a 2-3x increase in peak memory during multi-model warmups when legacy manifests triggered full eager hydration.
goals: 1) Implement a shard compactor that runs staged compaction/defragmentation post-ingest to reduce peak memory by 20-40% for common shard patterns. 2) Introduce a tokenizer-adapter registry so tokenizer state (vocab, merges, special tokens) can be initialized independently and cached across model variants. 3) Provide a one-shot migrator to normalize legacy manifests into the canonical manifest format and add validation hooks. 4) Remove direct tokenizer hydrating code paths from the weight activation critical path.
non_goals: Full redesign of the model registry or addressing runtime scheduling policies (that is separate work). This ticket does not change serving routing logic, model version rollout UI, or provide a new on-disk checkpoint format — it normalizes and compacts existing formats and adapters.
proposal:
A three-part approach:
1) Shard Compactor Service: lightweight background service that takes newly ingested weight shards and performs compaction passes. Compactor outputs a compacted shard with a fingerprint and checksum. Compaction runs in two modes: fast-pass (low CPU, moderate compaction) and deep-pass (higher CPU, better compaction) with configurable TTLs. The service will be integrated into the ingestion pipeline as a post-commit job and expose metrics (compaction_ratio, compaction_time, bytes_saved).

2) Tokenizer Adapter Registry: extract tokenizer init into a standalone adapter interface with a small lifecycle API: load_meta(), warm_kv(), checkout(). Implement adapters for BPE, unigram, SentencePiece, and a lightweight passthru adapter for byte-level tokenizers. The registry will maintain a cache keyed by (tokenizer-id, model-shape) and support LRU eviction and shared memory for co-located processes.

3) Manifest Normalizer & Migration: single CLI tool and pipeline step that converts legacy manifests to canonical_manifest_v2 (fields: weights, shards, checksums, tokenizer_ref, compacted_hint, activation_policy). Add validation to the ingest CI and a backward-compat shim that maps old fields at runtime while we complete migrations.
migration_plan: Phase 1 (2 weeks): Build tokenizer-adapter registry with a passthru and BPE adapter. Add unit tests and integration tests that run tokenizer init separately from weight load. Deploy behind a feature flag to canary infra. Phase 2 (2 weeks): Implement shard compactor (fast-pass) and wire as asynchronous post-commit job. Monitor compaction metrics and memory usage on canaries. Phase 3 (1 week): Implement manifest normalizer CLI and start converting a small set of less-critical models (>10% of traffic) via rolling migrations. Phase 4 (1 week): Enable the tokenizer registry as default; remove inlined tokenizer hydration in the activation path. Phase 5 (buffer week): Deep compaction and cleanup, deprecate legacy code paths and land follow-up tech-debt tickets.
testing_acceptance_criteria: 1) Cold-start p95 latency for model ingest reduced by >=15% on canary cluster. 2) Peak memory during multi-model warmup reduced by >=20% for test corpus. 3) Tokenizer initialization time is visible in metrics and decoupled from weight activation: end-to-end activation path shows tokenizer time <10% of total. 4) Compacted shards pass checksum validation and can be served interchangeably with original shards. 5) Migration tool has zero-diff semantics for a subset of canonical manifests and is covered by integration tests. 6) No increased error rate in smoke tests for 48 hours post-rollout.
rollout_plan:
- Start with internal canaries: 3 instances in staging with low-traffic models.
- Monitor compaction and tokenizer registry metrics: compaction_ratio, compaction_errors, tokenizer_cache_hit, activation_latency.
- After 72 hours and meeting acceptance criteria, expand to non-enterprise prod region (us-west-2) at 5% traffic.
- If stable for 7 days, gradually ramp to 50% and then full rollout.
- After full rollout, schedule a tech-debt cleanup sprint to remove legacy loader branches.
performance_targets:
- Reduce ingest cold-start p95 by 15-25% depending on model size.
- Reduce memory amplification during ingest by 20-40% on targeted models.
- Compaction fast-pass should complete within 30s for shards <=8GB; deep-pass target within 5m for shards <=32GB.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Compaction may temporarily increase IO and CPU leading to ingestion slowdowns. Mitigation: rate-limit compactor, run in background with backpressure to activation queue. Risk: Tokenizer cache correctness across model variants. Mitigation: strong checksum on tokenizer meta and integration tests with token-output equivalence. Risk: Migration introduces subtle manifest mismatches. Mitigation: keep backward-compat shim for 8 weeks and run conversion on low-traffic models first.
